item: MBAT reference mission (Main Belt Asteroid Tour, SEP)
value: 7.5 kW EOL power at 1.5 AU; 6-yr design life; dry mass 560 kg
location_in_source: Sec 'Analysis Cases' ('The MBAT mission was chosen because it is a relatively high power mission using solar electric propulsion... Location 1.5 AU')
notes: OUR EXACT MISSION CLASS: peer-reviewed parametric study of an SEP main-belt tour — the first independent W/kg anchor for our deep-space PV rows, in the same heliocentric band Module 4 operates in

item: Total array mass + EOL power, MBAT (4-junction GaAs case)
location_in_source: Sec Results ('normalized to the 4-j junction GaAs case (121 kg... $14.1M total array mass and cost)') + Sec Analysis Cases (EOL power required 7.5 kW at 1.5 AU)
notes: the two stated numbers; specific power is derived: ~62 W/kg in its FLIGHT environment (EOL, 1.5 AU). Converted to a 1-AU basis for the same hardware: x(1.5)^2 ~ 140 W/kg ARRAY-ONLY at 1 AU - vs our SYSTEM-level row of 60 W/kg @ 1 AU which must also carry PMAD + battery. That ratio (~2x) independently corroborates our row's own internal logic ('batteries, regulation and structure roughly halve that at the system level'): an array-only figure is ~2x a system figure, and this peer-reviewed study shows exactly that for hardware in our mission class

item: Total array cost + EOL power, MBAT (4-junction GaAs case)
location_in_source: Sec Results ('...$14.1M total array mass and cost')
notes: derived: ~$1880/W array-level in 2000 dollars, vs cell-level costs stated in the same study (4-j GaAs $400/W, thin-Si $220/W, CIS2 film ~$60/W) - ancillaries roughly quadruple cell cost at the array level; context for our solar $/W pricing rows

item: Thin-film efficiency needed to match crystalline array mass / cost
location_in_source: Sec Discussion ('a moderate thin-film cell efficiency of 12% is necessary to match the total mass... The cost breakpoint for the thin-film arrays occurs at thin-film efficiencies greater than 12%, resulting in an array that costs about half as much')
notes: the quantitative basis behind roll-out (ROSA-class) wings: below ~12% film efficiency, lightweight substrate alone does NOT win on mass — useful when evaluating future solar-row updates toward ROSA's ~150 W/kg wing figure our row currently cites without a source

item: Array-level vs blanket-level specific power divergence
value: blanket scales linearly with cell efficiency; total-array level much less rapid
location_in_source: Sec Discussion ('at the total array level, which includes array wiring, structures, mechanisms and a single-axis drive actuator... the increase is not linear')
notes: why our row is SYSTEM-level: 'ancillaries' (mechanisms, SADA, structure) are the dominant mass term at low film efficiency — any future wing-only W/kg figure must be de-rated by this effect before being compared to system rows
